name: IN-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+18 partisan lean makes this among the most Republican House seats
Incumbent Messmer holds a roughly 3-to-1 fundraising edge and over five times the cash on hand
No public polls or expert ratings; prediction markets price the Republican at about 94%
Challenger Allen's modest $108,000 in cash limits her ability to compete
model.rationale: An R+18 district with a well-funded incumbent leaves Mary Allen without a visible path; Messmer's money advantage, the absence of any polling attention or outside spending, and markets pricing the race at 94% Republican all point to a comfortable hold.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Messmer or an unexpected scandal could narrow the race, but no such signs have emerged.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 8th District sits about 18 points to the right of the nation as a whole, making it one of the more Republican-leaning House seats on the ballot. First-term incumbent Mark Messmer is running for re-election with a clear financial edge, having raised roughly $1.4 million to Democrat Mary Allen's $490,000, and he enters the final stretch with more than five times her cash on hand.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and campaign money. Prediction markets price Messmer's chances at about 94 percent, and there are no signs of competitive outside spending or sustained attention to the challenger. Absent a dramatic shift, the seat remains firmly in Republican hands heading into Election Day.
